claims.text: Introducing a secondary phase through annealing or other processing can increase the coercive field of single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys.
The initial material is single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
Elevated-temperature annealing can induce a secondary phase in the target FeCoNi alloy.
Annealing near 1000 °C under argon is a relevant processing condition for the proposed intervention.
Processing may form a B2 or sigma secondary phase at grain boundaries or within the matrix.
The secondary phase creates domain-wall pinning sites.
Domain-wall pinning hinders domain-wall motion and thereby increases coercivity.
The intervention will increase coercive field relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative.
The resulting coercive field may exceed 100 Oe.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has a coercive field no greater than 100 Oe.
Excessive phase separation or undesired phases could negatively affect magnetic properties.
The cited annealed AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi alloy formed sigma phase at grain boundaries and exhibited increased coercivity.
The optimal processing conditions and secondary-phase composition for maximizing coercivity are unknown.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome only says that exceeding 100 Oe is possible, whereas the falsification rule treats failure to exceed 100 Oe as falsifying the whole hypothesis. An increase that remains below 100 Oe would support the primary predicted direction but be classified as falsification.
